The agent can start a stream on an emulator or a USB-connected phone, build and install a Gradle p"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"roject, drive the UI by `resource-id`/text or by OCR, read logcat, and inspect processes and memory,"},{"id":"p9s4","text":" while a live stream of the device renders in a persistent sidebar panel where you can tap, drag, ro"},{"id":"p9s5","text":"tate, and press Back / Home / Recents directly on the video. No image blocks and no screen-recording"},{"id":"p9s6","text":" files: visual bytes reach the UI only through signed, expiring URLs served by the DSH webserver."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"There is exactly one code path. `adb devices -l` reports a **serial**, and that serial is a device's"},{"id":"p10s2","text":" only identity — `emulator-5554`, a USB serial, or an `ip:port` target all behave identically. The p"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"lugin is bound to no emulator product (AVD, Genymotion, WSA, a cloud device farm), and there is no s"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"imulator/real-device split to reason about."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"| 📱 **Live device in the conversation** | A `multipart/x-mixed-replace` PNG stream produced **in-pro"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"cess** and served straight from the latest-frame buffer through signed `/_dsh/dsh-android/*` routes."},{"id":"p11s3","text":" |
| 🔌 **No external stream helper, no inner port** | One persistent `adb exec-out` child runs `whil"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"e :; do screencap -p; done`; the host splits the concatenated PNGs into frames itself. There is no l"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"oopback stream server to proxy, no port range to manage, and nothing to adopt after an ungraceful ex"},{"id":"p11s6","text":"it. |
| 🧩 **One adb code path** | Emulators and phones are the same thing to adb and to this plugin."},{"id":"p11s7","text":" No `simctl`/WebDriverAgent dual stack, no build-and-trust dance before a physical device works. |
|"},{"id":"p11s8","text":" 🛠️ **20 agent tools** | Devices, boot/shutdown, screenshot, interact, Gradle build & run, app listi"},{"id":"p11s9","text":"ng/launching, `uiautomator` UI tree + tap-by-element, list/feed row actions, Vision OCR find/tap/wai"},{"id":"p11s10","text":"t, logcat, processes, ANR/crash backtrace, meminfo, app info. |
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- **The browser never talks to adb, and there is no inner port to talk to.** The stream is produced "},{"id":"p13s2","text":"in this process and served from memory; every byte crosses the DSH webserver origin through plugin-o"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"wned `/_dsh/dsh-android/*` routes: `/stream/<token>` (live multipart PNG), `/screenshot/<token>` (ca"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"ched PNG), plus `/grant`, `/switch-device`, `/devices`, `/capture`, `/status`, `/control`, and `/dev"},{"id":"p13s5","text":"ice-action`. This is a strictly smaller attack surface than a proxied loopback stream server.
- **A "},{"id":"p13s6","text":"triple loopback fence by default, applied before any capability is read.** The transport peer must b"},{"id":"p13s7","text":"e a loopback address, the `Host` header must name a loopback authority (so a DNS-rebinding `Host` is"},{"id":"p13s8","text":" rejected), and Fetch-Metadata/`Origin` must be same-origin. Host and Origin are caller-controlled d"},{"id":"p13s9","text":"ata and are never trusted on their own.
- **`trustedAuthorities` for deployments reached through a r"},{"id":"p13s10","text":"everse proxy.** A loopback peer proves the last hop came from this machine, which is always true beh"},{"id":"p13s11","text":"ind a proxy — while the `Host` the proxy forwards is the deployment's public name, so every route ab"},{"id":"p13s12","text":"ove answers 403 and the plugin only works through an SSH tunnel. The optional config accepts those a"},{"id":"p13s13","text":"uthorities explicitly, the way DSH's own `--trusted-host` does for its webserver:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"An entry may be a bare `host`, a `host:port`, or a pasted origin, and what it covers is decided by w"},{"id":"p15s2","text":" be a bare `host`, a `host:port`, or a pasted origin, and what it covers is decided by what it says:"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"| Entry | Matches | `Origin` accepted |"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"| `host` | that hostname on any Host port | that host on HTTP 80 or HTTPS 443 |
| `host:port` | `Hos"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"t: host:port` | that port on `http` or `https` |
| `https://host` | that hostname on any Host port |"},{"id":"p17s3","text":" HTTPS on that host, port 443 |
| `https://host:port` | `Host: host:port` | `https` on that port onl"},{"id":"p17s4","text":"TPS on that host, port 443 |
| `https://host:port` | `Host: host:port` | `https` on that port only |"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"- **Node ≥ 24.11.0.**
- **adb**, from the Android SDK platform-tools, resolved in this order: the `A"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"DB` environment variable → `adb` on `PATH` → `<ANDROID_HOME>`/`<ANDROID_SDK_ROOT>`/the per-OS defaul"},{"id":"p20s3","text":"t SDK root + `/platform-tools/adb`. Install it with `sdkmanager "platform-tools"`, with Android Stud"},{"id":"p20s4","text":"io, or with `brew install --cask android-platform-tools`. Without adb the plugin still loads and all"},{"id":"p20s5","text":" 20 tools register; every call then explains what is missing.
- **A device**: an emulator of any pro"},{"id":"p20s6","text":"duct, or a phone with USB debugging enabled. The `emulator` launcher is optional and only `android_b"},{"id":"p20s7","text":"oot`-by-AVD-name needs it — everything else works with whatever adb can see.
- **DSH ≥ 0.1.0-rc.6 wi"},{"id":"p20s8","text":"th the web bundle** for the panel. Headless profiles work too: all 20 tools function normally, just "},{"id":"p20s9","text":"without the live view.
- **macOS host for OCR** (only `android_find_text` / `android_tap_text` / `an"},{"id":"p20s10","text":"droid_wait_for` need it): the plugin compiles its bundled `assets/ocr.swift` with `swiftc` on first "},{"id":"p20s11","text":"use into `~/Library/Caches/dsh-android/bin/ocr`. On Linux and Windows hosts those three tools report"},{"id":"p20s12","text":" that OCR needs the macOS Vision framework; the other 17 are unaffected. Overrides: `DSHPLUGIN_ANDRO"},{"id":"p20s13","text":"ID_OCR_DIR`, `DSHPLUGIN_ANDROID_OCR_SWIFT`, `DSHPLUGIN_ANDROID_SWIFTC`.
- **ADBKeyboard** (optional,"},{"id":"p20s14","text":" for CJK and emoji input): `adb shell input text` is ASCII-only. Install ADBKeyboard on the device a"},{"id":"p20s15","text":"nd select it as the active IME, and non-ASCII text is delivered through its broadcast interface. Wit"},{"id":"p20s16","text":"hout it, non-ASCII typing is REFUSED with the install hint — never silently mistyped."}],"truncated":true}
